title: Sum over bounded Hermite indices
statement: Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, let $E$ be an additive commutative monoid, and assign an element $v(\alpha)\in E$ to each function $\alpha\colon\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\mathbb N$. The sum of $v(\alpha)$ over all such indices with $\sum_i\alpha(i)\le k$ equals the sum over all coordinate choices $a(i)\in\{0,\ldots,k\}$, retaining $v(a)$ when $\sum_i a(i)\le k$ and contributing zero otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: $v$ assigns an element of $E$ to each natural-valued index function
